claims.text: Two consecutive releases of the site pushed cleanly, verified themselves against both remotes, and never reached anybody.
claims.quote: Two consecutive releases of this site pushed cleanly, verified themselves against both remotes

claims.text: The site served a two-release-old page for forty minutes.
claims.quote: The site served a two-release-old page for forty minutes.

claims.text: The failure was noticed by a human on a phone who looked at the version badge.
claims.quote: It was noticed by a human on a phone, who looked at the version badge

claims.text: The checks were not weak; they were checking the wrong boundary.
claims.quote: The checks were not weak. They were checking the wrong boundary.

claims.text: The release script does five things and four of them are good: build, validate, push the encrypted vault, push the git mirror and confirm it is in sync.
claims.quote: The release script does five things, and four of them are good

claims.text: Confirming HEAD equals origin/dev compares hashes and means the bytes arrived at GitHub; it does not mean anybody can read them.
claims.quote: It means the bytes arrived at GitHub. It does not mean anybody can read them.

claims.text: Publishing the site has three boundaries, source to git remote to Pages deploy to the reader, and only two were verified.
claims.quote: Publishing this site has three boundaries, and we were verifying two

claims.text: The deploy job died in Set up job because codeload.github.com rate-limited the download of a third-party action with a 429.
claims.quote: rate-limited the download of a third-party action

claims.text: The validate and tag-release jobs passed; the one job that puts bytes in front of readers could not fetch its own dependency.
claims.quote: The one job that puts bytes in front of readers could not fetch its own dependency.

claims.text: The most likely thing to break in a deploy is not your code but shared infrastructure you do not run.
claims.quote: the most likely thing to break in a deploy is not your code.

claims.text: A release now finishes by asking the live site what version it is serving, polling with a cache-buster for up to eight minutes.
claims.quote: A release now finishes by asking the live site what version it is serving

claims.text: If the version never appears the release aborts loudly, names the Actions page, and says a 429 on the action download is transient and needs a re-run.
claims.quote: If the version never appears it aborts loudly, names the Actions page

claims.text: The cost of the check is up to eight minutes of waiting on every release.
claims.quote: The cost is real: up to eight minutes of waiting on every release.

claims.text: The site has three rules of one shape: a page nothing links to, a page the machine index omits, and a page the deploy never served are all unpublished.
claims.quote: A page the deploy never served is unpublished.

claims.text: Shipped is a fact about the reader, not about your repository.
claims.quote: shipped is a fact about the reader, not about your repository.

claims.text: Each of the three rules was learned by getting it wrong first, which is why the list is short and specific.
claims.quote: Every one of them was learned by getting it wrong first

claims.text: The check detects a failed deploy; it does not repair one, and a 429 still needs a human or a re-run.
claims.quote: It detects a failed deploy; it does not repair one.

claims.text: The check reads the home page's version badge, not every page, so a partial deploy that published some files would pass.
claims.quote: It checks the home page's version badge, not every page.

claims.text: The check adds up to eight minutes to a release, a real tax on small fixes.
claims.quote: It adds up to eight minutes to a release, which is a real tax on small fixes.

claims.text: The release script is in the SGit-AI__CLI repository and the releases described are v0.2.31 to v0.2.33.
claims.quote: the releases described here are v0.2.31 to v0.2.33
